description:
Add get_tree/1 to SessionManager. It builds the full session tree as a list of root
OctoPi.Coder.Session.TreeNode structs, resolving labels from the label maps built in opi-iu9.9.

## Spec

```elixir
@spec get_tree(t()) :: [TreeNode.t()]
def get_tree(%__MODULE__{} = sm)
```

## Algorithm

Mirror getTree() lines 1075-1115 in session-manager.ts:

1. Call get_entries(sm) to get all body entries (excluding header).
2. For each entry, create:
   %TreeNode{
     entry: entry,
     children: [],
     label: Map.get(sm.labels_by_id, entry.id),
     label_timestamp: Map.get(sm.label_timestamps_by_id, entry.id)
   }
3. Build the tree by parent_id linking (same as existing build_tree/1 in the component,
   which is a known-good implementation to copy from). Orphans become roots.
4. Sort children by timestamp ascending (oldest first, newest at bottom).
   Mirrors the sort in getTree() lines 1107-1112.

## Notes

- This function depends on TreeNode being in OctoPi.Coder.Session.TreeNode (opi-iu9.8) and
  on labels_by_id being present (opi-iu9.9).
- The existing Tree.build_tree/1 in the component layer does not resolve labels and does
  not sort children by timestamp. It can remain as-is for tests that do not need labels;
  the TUI layer will switch to calling get_tree/1 via the Coder interface (opi-iu9.11).

## Files
apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/session_manager.ex

## Tests
- get_tree/1 on an empty session returns [].
- get_tree/1 on a linear session returns a single root chain.
- get_tree/1 on a branched session returns multiple children at branch points.
- Labels are present on nodes where the label map has an entry; nil elsewhere.
- Children are sorted by timestamp (oldest first).
Port relevant cases from tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/labels.test.ts
and test/session-manager/tree-traversal.test.ts.
